column1: # tests/partlayout/writers.tsv -- the HAND CLASS MAP of every function that
# carries an inline/linkage attribute in an emitted artifact (docs/design/
# compound_entries.md §3.1, §3.6 "the attribute census"). Each row names its
# WRITER, the attribute KIND it may write, and the function NAMES it writes
# them on (an ERE over the name with the artifact prefix replaced by `P`).
# A function that carries an attribute and matches no row of its kind is an
# unlisted writer, and the census FAILS naming it: a new writer must be
# added here with its owner, never discovered.
# kind: `always_inline`, `noinline` or `noipa` (on the definition line, or on
# a line of its own above it: the guarded `shared` block), `noclone` (the
# search head's guarded `__attribute__((noclone))` line above a definition),
# `static-inline` (a `static inline` definition with no other attribute).
# text: where the writer's attribute TEXT comes from. `PCREC_ATTR_X` is a row
# the writer keeps its decision and asks the table for the text. `own` is a
# writer that spells its text itself (the plain `static inline` writers
# A4-A7, out of [ATTR-TABLE]'s scope). The census checks every `PCREC_ATTR_X`
# named here is a row of the table.
